back2basics.text: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a government-guaranteed price at which it procures certain crops from farmers to ensure income stability. back2basics.concept: UN Climate Change Conferences (COP) and Consensus Decision-Making
back2basics.text: The Conference of Parties (COP) is an annual UN meeting where countries negotiate climate action under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. Decisions require consensus, meaning all parties must agree on the text. This ensures inclusivity but can lead to deadlocks if countries have conflicting interests, especially on sensitive issues like fossil fuel use and climate finance.

2026-11-25-pm-37a12f0de9.deck: COP31 in Turkiye concluded without a consensus climate agreement due to disagreements on fossil fuel phase-out language. This outcome highlights the challenges in global climate negotiations and India's position on balancing climate goals with developmental needs.

body.label: Fossil fuel phase-out disagreement
body.text: The main cause was a standoff over including explicit language on fossil fuel phase-out in the final consensus cover text, with the EU and around 130 countries rejecting the text for lacking this.

body.label: Opposing country positions
body.text: The EU and Panama opposed the cover text, accusing it of greenwashing fossil fuels and weakening previous commitments, while India, China, and Saudi Arabia supported the text to maintain fossil fuel use for economic reasons.

body.label: Consensus requirement
body.text: The UN climate talks require unanimous agreement on the final text, so objections by a large group prevented any consensus deal.

sections.heading: What caused COP31 to end without a climate deal?

body.label: Science and temperature targets
body.text: The EU and others argued that without fossil fuel phase-out commitments, the talks fail to align with scientific goals to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

body.label: Equity and responsibility concerns
body.text: Developing countries like India and LMDC coalition members emphasized equity, historical responsibility of developed nations, and the need for climate action to be nationally determined and supported by finance and technology.

body.label: Impact on global climate governance
body.text: The failure to reach consensus exposes the difficulty of multilateral climate action when countries have divergent economic priorities and responsibilities.

sections.heading: Why does the fossil fuel phase-out debate matter for climate action?

body.label: Focus on implementation means
body.text: India stressed that climate ambition must be matched with means of implementation, including finance, technology, and capacity-building for developing countries.

body.label: Role in shaping outcome
body.text: India influenced the outcome on issues like food security, livelihoods, and methane action, reflecting its priorities in climate negotiations.

body.label: Definition and purpose
body.text: The VRR auction is a tool used by RBI to borrow funds from banks for a short tenor of one day at variable interest rates, helping manage liquidity in the banking system.

body.label: Recent auction details
body.text: On November 25, 2026, RBI notified an amount of ₹50,000 crore for the VRR auction, received bids worth ₹1,62,017 crore, and allotted ₹50,007 crore at a cut-off rate of 5.66%.

body.label: Partial allotment
body.text: Only about 50.55% of the bids received at the cut-off rate were allotted, indicating RBI's selective absorption of liquidity.

sections.heading: What is the Overnight Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction?

body.label: Money market segments
body.text: RBI monitors various segments like call money, triparty repo, market repo, and repo in corporate bonds to gauge liquidity and interest rates.

body.label: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)
body.text: RBI conducts repo and reverse repo operations under LAF to inject or absorb liquidity; for example, on November 23, 2026, RBI conducted fixed and variable rate repo operations totaling over ₹1 lakh crore.

body.label: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)
body.text: SDF and MSF are additional tools used by RBI to absorb or provide liquidity; on November 23 and 24, 2026, RBI absorbed liquidity through these facilities at rates of 5.25% and 5.75% respectively.

body.label: Net liquidity position
body.text: On November 23, 2026, RBI's net liquidity injection including outstanding operations was ₹6,401.26 crore, while on November 24, 2026, it was ₹12,825.26 crore, showing active liquidity management.

sections.heading: How does RBI manage liquidity through money market operations?

back2basics.concept: Election Commission of India and Electoral Rolls
back2basics.text: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for administering elections and maintaining electoral rolls. Electoral rolls are lists of eligible voters, which are periodically updated through processes like the Special Intensive Revision to ensure accuracy and inclusion of new voters. Decisions by the Commission are ideally collective to maintain transparency and trust in democratic processes.

body.text: The ₹11,000-crore scheme approved by the Cabinet will run for eight years from FY2026-27 to FY2033-34 to develop indigenous manufacturing capacity in Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE).

body.text: It includes a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year to settle incentives for incremental sales.

back2basics.concept: National Security and Corporate Governance in Tech
back2basics.text: National security concerns can arise when technology companies operate in sensitive sectors or have leadership linked to foreign entities. Corporate governance involves oversight by a company's board to ensure ethical conduct and compliance with laws. When allegations of espionage or conflicts of interest emerge, governments may intervene to protect national interests, especially in strategic industries like AI chip manufacturing.

back2basics.text: The principle of natural justice requires that a person must be given a fair hearing before any adverse action is taken against them. This includes the right to be informed of allegations and the opportunity to present their case. Courts must provide reasons for their decisions, especially when directing investigations, to prevent arbitrary or unjust actions.

2026-11-25-pm-d865989d30.deck: The Supreme Court set aside the Allahabad High Court's interim orders directing CBI and ED investigations into a disproportionate assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi, emphasizing procedural fairness. back2basics.text: Electoral roll revision is the process of updating the list of eligible voters to ensure accuracy and remove duplicates or ineligible entries. Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a focused exercise to clean the electoral rolls comprehensively. The Election Commission of India oversees this process to maintain free and fair elections, but it must balance transparency, accuracy, and federal cooperation.
